correctness.rationale: Inverse-affine mapping proves all area maximizers are images of equilateral circle triangles. Exact side lengths s_i and tangential derivative D_i identify a vertex with |D_i| bounded below by 9 b²(a²-b²)/(16a⁴) using trigonometric range and Heron. A bounded second derivative and a chosen signed angular step give a concrete gain at least 81 b⁷(a²-b²)²/(2048a¹⁰), uniformly for each area-maximizer. Near a=1+ε,b=1 the transverse Hessian around equilateral triples is negative definite, linear εδ term is explicit and completing square yields coefficient 9sqrt(3)/16. Independent 600 numerical derivatives matched analytic first variation to <8e-15; independent multi-eccentricity global optimizations showed normalized near-circle gap increasing toward 0.974278579, not used to prove the asymptotic. Globality near circle follows compactness of circular equilateral maximizers and uniform transverse Hessian.

originality.rationale: The full published Resultary theorem “Exact perimeter selection among maximum-area polygons inscribed in ellipses” classifies rotations only within the maximum-area family, explicitly excluding all-inscribed perimeter maximization. It cannot imply a positive gap to the unrestricted maximum or the claimed ε² coefficient. Hoehner treats many-vertex asymptotic simultaneous intrinsic-volume optimization; a fixed three-vertex quantitative inequality is not a corollary. Classical ellipse billiards only gives first-order reflection stationarity. No matching all-eccentricity bound or local coefficient found; historical elliptic-integral priority remains possible.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed local elliptic integral/billiard perturbation may contain the same quadratic coefficient.
